title: Characterization of Exponentially Modified Gaussian Peaks in Chromatography

citations.claim: Grushka defined the exponentially modified Gaussian (EMG) peak as the convolution of a Gaussian function with an exponential decay, providing a theoretically justified model for chromatographic peak shapes that accounts for extra-column band broadening.

The EMG peak shape is parameterized by the Gaussian standard deviation sigma, the retention time tR, and the exponential time constant tau, where the ratio tau/sigma controls the degree of peak asymmetry.

Grushka derived closed-form expressions for the first four statistical moments of the EMG peak: the first moment is M1 = tR + tau, the second central moment is M2 = sigma^2 + tau^2, and the third central moment is M3 = 2*tau^3.

The skewness of an EMG peak ranges from 0 (pure Gaussian, tau/sigma = 0) to 2.0 (pure exponential decay, tau/sigma approaching infinity), with the fastest change occurring at tau/sigma approximately equal to 0.81.

Extra-column contributions such as detector dead volume and mixing chambers exponentially modify the chromatographic peak, with each source characterized by a specific time constant that determines the extent of peak distortion.

The EMG model is widely used as a realistic synthetic peak shape for generating training data in chromatographic signal processing, owing to its theoretical justification and ability to reproduce the asymmetric tailing commonly observed in real chromatograms.

do_not_claim: Grushka proposed the EMG model for baseline correction
Grushka applied deep learning or any computational learning method
The EMG model accounts for baseline drift or wandering baselines
Grushka was the first to use convolution of Gaussian and exponential functions in any context
